subject: Physics
cover: Light: mirror & lens formulas you must know

slides.headline: Mirror formula
slides.sub: 1/v + 1/u = 1/f  (v = image distance, u = object distance, f = focal length)

slides.headline: Magnification (mirror)
slides.sub: m = −v/u = height of image / height of object

slides.headline: Magnification (lens)
slides.sub: m = v/u = height of image / height of object

slides.headline: Power of a lens
slides.sub: P = 1/f (f in metres) · Unit: dioptre (D) · Convex = +, Concave = −

slides.headline: Refractive index
slides.sub: n = speed of light in vacuum / speed in medium = sin i / sin r

subject: Physics
cover: Electricity: all the formulas in one place

slides.headline: Ohm's Law
slides.sub: V = I × R  (V = voltage, I = current, R = resistance)

slides.headline: Electric power
slides.sub: P = VI = I²R = V²/R · Unit: watt (W)

slides.headline: Resistors in series
slides.sub: R = R₁ + R₂ + R₃ + … (total resistance increases)

slides.headline: Resistors in parallel
slides.sub: 1/R = 1/R₁ + 1/R₂ + 1/R₃ + … (total resistance decreases)

slides.headline: Electrical energy
slides.sub: E = P × t · Commercial unit = kilowatt-hour (kWh) = 3.6 × 10⁶ J

subject: Physics
cover: The human eye & how to correct its defects

slides.headline: Near & far point
slides.sub: Normal near point = 25 cm · Far point = infinity

slides.headline: Myopia (short-sightedness)
slides.sub: Can't see distant objects clearly · Corrected using a concave (diverging) lens

slides.headline: Hypermetropia (long-sightedness)
slides.sub: Can't see near objects clearly · Corrected using a convex (converging) lens

slides.headline: Power of accommodation
slides.sub: The eye lens changes its focal length to focus on near and far objects.

slides.headline: The pH scale
slides.sub: 0 to 14 · pH < 7 = acidic · pH = 7 = neutral · pH > 7 = basic

slides.headline: Neutralisation
slides.sub: Acid + Base → Salt + Water (e.g., HCl + NaOH → NaCl + H₂O)

slides.headline: Acid + metal
slides.sub: Acid + Metal → Salt + Hydrogen gas

slides.headline: Acid + carbonate
slides.sub: Acid + Metal carbonate → Salt + Water + Carbon dioxide

slides.headline: Combination
slides.sub: Two or more substances combine into one (A + B → AB)

slides.headline: Decomposition
slides.sub: One substance breaks into two or more (AB → A + B)

slides.headline: Displacement
slides.sub: A more reactive element displaces a less reactive one (A + BC → AC + B)

slides.headline: Double displacement
slides.sub: Ions are exchanged between two compounds (AB + CD → AD + CB)

slides.headline: Oxidation & reduction (Redox)
slides.sub: Oxidation = gain of oxygen / loss of hydrogen · Reduction = the opposite

subject: Chemistry
cover: Carbon: why it forms so many compounds

slides.headline: Tetravalency
slides.sub: Carbon has 4 valence electrons, so it forms 4 covalent bonds.

slides.headline: Catenation
slides.sub: Carbon atoms link with each other to form long chains, branches and rings.

slides.headline: Covalent bonding
slides.sub: Carbon shares electrons (doesn't gain/lose), forming strong covalent bonds.

slides.headline: Homologous series
slides.sub: A series of compounds with the same general formula, differing by CH₂.

subject: Biology
cover: Life Processes: the 4 you must know

slides.headline: Nutrition
slides.sub: Autotrophic (plants make food via photosynthesis) · Heterotrophic (depend on others)

slides.headline: Photosynthesis
slides.sub: 6CO₂ + 6H₂O → (sunlight, chlorophyll) → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂

slides.headline: Respiration
slides.sub: Glucose breaks down to release energy · Aerobic (with O₂) gives more energy than anaerobic

slides.headline: Transportation
slides.sub: In humans: heart & blood · In plants: xylem carries water, phloem carries food

slides.headline: Traits
slides.sub: Characteristics passed from parents to offspring through genes.

slides.headline: Dominant vs recessive
slides.sub: A dominant trait shows even with one copy; a recessive trait needs two copies.

slides.headline: Genotype vs phenotype
slides.sub: Genotype = the genes (e.g., Tt) · Phenotype = the visible trait (e.g., tall)

slides.headline: Mendel's monohybrid ratio
slides.sub: Crossing Tt × Tt gives a 3 : 1 phenotype ratio in the F₂ generation.
